minutes.headline: ZBA granted special permits for a Cove Road addition's rear-setback and height relief, conditioned on Conservation and Board of Health approvals.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard one application from Brian and Katie Fox for an addition to a single-family home on Cove Road, needing relief on rear yard setback and building height. A neighbor raised septic, water line, stakes, trees and drainage concerns, and the applicant's engineer answered them. The board voted to grant the permit provisionally, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted special permits for rear yard setback and building height relief for a Cove Road home addition.
The grant is provisional, contingent on Conservation Commission and Board of Health approvals, with Board of Health requirements recorded with the building inspector.
The vote tally was not clearly audible in the recording; the chair declared the permit granted after calling the vote.
An abutter on Sandy Cove Road raised septic, water line, tree, stake and drainage concerns, and the applicants' engineer answered them.
The applicants agreed to place stakes showing the addition's location for the abutter; the board did not make this a formal condition.

why_it_matters: Relief from setback and height limits changes how close and how tall a house can stand next to its neighbors, and the permit only takes effect after a 14-day appeal window and recording at the registry of deeds.

The stakes were an agreement between the applicants and the abutter, not a condition of the permit, so a neighbor's drainage and septic concerns are addressed through the Conservation and Board of Health approvals rather than through the ZBA decision itself.
